system.net.bytes_rcvd.ref: vendor: fixtures/datadog/otel-mapping.yaml row system.net.bytes_rcvd -> system.network.io. datadog: integrations-core@a9b9e42 network/datadog_checks/network/check_linux.py reads /proc/net/dev; network.py submit_devicemetrics sends bytes_rcvd with self.rate per interface; network/metadata.csv gauge, unit byte/second. otel: fixtures/otel/collector-contrib/receiver/hostmetricsreceiver/internal/scraper/networkscraper/metadata.yaml system.network.io direction=receive, sum monotonic cumulative, unit By, per device; rate() gives By/s. dash0 (default, 2026-11-08): count by (otel_scope_name, system_network_direction, host_name) (last_over_time({otel_metric_name="system.network.io", otel_metric_type="sum"}[24h])) returned two emitters: hostmetrics networkscraper and Python opentelemetry.instrumentation.system_metrics (load-generator; same interface names, same host_name), so a plain sum double counts. The otel_scope_name matcher keeps the hostmetrics series. Loopback is kept: Datadog's network check excludes no interface by default (integrations-core@a9b9e42 network/datadog_checks/network/network.py: excluded_interfaces defaults to []; spec.yaml lists lo/lo0 only as an example), and the hostmetrics network scraper includes every interface unless configured. No grain (assumption, not reviewed): a max by (service_instance_id) would turn the sum over interfaces into a max; resource-hash duplicates were only observed on Postgres series. rateWindow 5m (issue #90): the target is reported every 60 s in Dash0 (count_over_time(...[10m]) = 10 per series on dataset default, 2026-11-07 20:27 UTC), too sparse for Dash0's $__rate_interval (the panel showed "No data" with a gaps warning asking for at least 120s); 5m covers 4+ samples.
